cover.imageDescription: Large unboxed gold brush lettering titles THE LOCK above ordinary middle-aged Stephen reaching with an open hand toward a translucent blue-white membrane and distant starfield architecture. A faint layer overlaps his forehead. Three smaller warm human scenes on the left show family at a table, Stephen helping a student and a quiet conversation over mugs, connected by fine gold lines. The lower-right tagline sits directly on dark artwork without a text plate.
cover.transcript:
TONE COMICS
THE LOCK
SOME DOORS OPEN ONLY WHEN FORGETTING STOPS.

page-01.imageDescription: A boy sits beneath a broad mountain night sky, gazing upward. Two moments of adolescence and younger adulthood: writing at a desk and looking through a window. Adult Stephen shares a table with a woman and child; a work-at-desk moment appears behind them. Middle-aged Stephen looks upward on a quiet suburban street. A small thought appears beside him. Seen from behind, Stephen stands small beneath a vast night sky while the neighbourhood continues around him.
page-01.transcript:
There was always something else.
Not a plan. Not a voice. Not even a belief.
Just the ache that ordinary life couldn’t quite be the whole story.
MOOOOORE.

page-02.imageDescription: Six panels follow Stephen from a young traveller overlooking a Chilean-style city beneath the Andes, to university with books, through an arched doorway, to a tired evening at his desk, then into a simple retreat among eucalyptus. The final wide panel shows an older Stephen seated quietly in an unadorned room beside a mountain-view window. A fine gold thread links the montage; four small narration captions leave faces and gestures clear.
page-02.transcript:
My life rarely arrived as a map.
A door appeared.
I walked through.
Then another.

page-03.imageDescription: Six warm, intimate panels show Stephen pouring coffee, listening to a woman at a kitchen table, sitting beside a puzzled student, pointing to a passage, watching the student resume writing, and sharing a small laugh with a woman colleague. Small ivory narration captions leave the faces and gestures clear. Stephen remains an ordinary middle-aged man in a dark hoodie or navy overshirt.
page-03.transcript:
I never became the man with the grand mission.
Mostly, I listened.
Explained.
Helped things settle.

page-04.imageDescription: Stephen lies in bed at night with eyes closed. A closer panel shows concentration without panic; beside it, delicate blue-white and violet curved lines overlap his forehead. He sits up and quietly asks what it is in a small mouth-tailed speech balloon. The large final wordless profile shows the same subtle membrane and the ordinary bedroom still present behind him.
page-04.transcript:
Then there was the block.
Not fear exactly.
More like an invisible wall that cancelled momentum.
What the hell is that?

page-05.imageDescription: Seven panels show Stephen reading at a laptop at night, a close view of five starseed-related words on its physical screen, blue screen reflections in his eyes, a mild eye-roll, a hand on the trackpad, a dry inward reaction in a dotted thought balloon, and a quieter look back toward the computer. Small narration captions frame the scene; the room remains ordinary and no outside being appears.
page-05.transcript:
Then the internet became very normal.
volunteer
Pleiades
veil
hold the light
grounded antenna
Yeah, sure. Pleiadian starseed. Completely reasonable.
Annoyingly, some of it pressed exactly the right buttons.

page-06.imageDescription: Stephen sits quietly on his bed after waking, looking toward the window. His inward question appears in a thought balloon. Close-up of Stephen looking down; a small tailless inner answer sits in open space. Stephen turns his gaze, asking a second inward question in a dotted thought balloon. Stephen in profile at the left of a quiet panel; the second lowercase inner answer occupies open space to the right. A wide wordless view of Stephen seated on the bed, with soft light entering through the city-facing window.
page-06.transcript:
Is there actually a lock?
yes.
Why?
to keep you grounded.

page-07.imageDescription: Nine ink-drawn panels. In three bedroom close-ups, middle-aged Stephen asks inwardly, receives the small answer life, and gives a wry sideways glance. The wordless montage then shows him pouring coffee with family, driving through rainy traffic, helping a tired student with an open book, carrying groceries in rain, unpacking them in the kitchen and laughing over dinner with family. Dark navy and warm household light keep the scenes ordinary and human.
page-07.transcript:
What needs to happen before the lock changes?
life.
...Helpful.

page-08.imageDescription: Three narrow upper panels show Stephen sitting on his bed with an inward question, a quiet profile beside the window receiving view, and a subtly surprised expression beneath a small narration caption. A large wordless panel below opens onto the same ordinary bedroom: Stephen sits at the bed's edge looking toward the city window; a lamp, framed pictures, books, desk, chair and rug remain in soft morning light.
page-08.transcript:
What am I supposed to understand right now?
view.
That one landed differently.

page-09.imageDescription: Four tight upper panels show Stephen seated on his bed touching his throat, a worried close-up of his eyes, his fingers against his neck beside tangled dark marks, and his head beginning to turn. In the larger lower panel, a fine gold resonance arc and the unboxed GOOOOONG sweep through the ordinary room. Stephen turns toward the wider room while his hand remains near his throat; his expression is attentive, not euphoric.
page-09.transcript:
Under pressure, I forgot everything complicated.
But one thing survived.
GOOOOONG
And the head turned.

page-10.imageDescription: A full-page bedroom scene shows Stephen sitting barefoot on the bed while fine gold and pale-blue threads continue across him, the furniture, window and surrounding space. Four small insets show an eye reflecting the window, an ear and profile, fingers at the throat, and a quiet thoughtful face. Three small narration captions descend into a fading final caption; the lower room imagery becomes wordless. Stephen remains ordinary and seated, not emitting or controlling the field.
page-10.transcript:
Waveform.
Seeing. Hearing. Throat. Thought. Space. All at once.
Then even the word wasn’t needed.

page-11.imageDescription: Five panels move from Stephen touching his throat and frowning, to his seated body and ordinary bedroom details. Pale blue lines share the body, thoughts, curtain, glass and sounds. The large borderless final room contains a cropped resting hand at lower left but no central observing person.
page-11.transcript:
The throat could throat.
Thought could think.
Even the story about getting free was part of the display.
Nothing had to be thrown out first.

page-12.imageDescription: A wide bedroom panel shows Stephen relaxing with open hands. Two middle panels show him noticing the relief, then looking at a half-closing hand with a small thought balloon. Three tighter bottom frames show a tiny grasping line-metaphor between fingers, his face inside nested borders, and a quiet rueful half-smile as he sits in the room again.
page-12.transcript:
Then relief arrived.
So naturally...
Keep this.
And there I was again.

page-13.imageDescription: Six curved interlocking vignettes show Stephen ruminating at his desk, looking up in recollection, becoming caught in thought again, walking on an ordinary wet street, making coffee, and sitting by a window. A slender gold spiral winds through the page around a small central ripple; small blue-white ripples suggest the remembered cue without a physical gong.
page-13.transcript:
Forget.
Remember.
Forget again.
Not a straight path.
A spiral.

page-14.imageDescription: Stephen listens across an office desk to a young adult student. A close-up shows the student's overloaded thoughts as fine tangled lines; Stephen then points calmly to paperwork. The student leaves with a little more ease. Stephen listens to an adult family member over coffee. A wide final shared workspace shows people talking normally, joined by very fine gold relational lines, while Stephen remains an ordinary participant.
page-14.transcript:
Long before the mythology, there was a simpler pattern.
People arrived tangled.
Sometimes they left with a little more room.
Ambient stabiliser.

page-15.imageDescription: Stephen waits among ordinary commuters beside a tram, both feet on the pavement and hands in pockets. A thread-thin vertical line passes through him from sky to ground. Three bottom insets show coffee-making, helping with paperwork and washing a cup.
page-15.transcript:
Grounded antenna.
Maybe the grounding wasn’t the thing stopping the signal.
Maybe it was what made the signal usable.

page-16.imageDescription: Six warm close panels show Stephen listening to an anxious young adult, a frustrated family member, an unsure student and a tired colleague. A close-up holds on the anxious person's hand near their chin; in the final couch scene that person opens a hand and visibly exhales while Stephen listens. Backgrounds become quieter and more open.
page-16.transcript:
Maybe sanctuary isn’t somewhere you go.
Maybe sometimes it’s the few minutes another person doesn’t have to defend themselves.

page-17.imageDescription: Four broad panels show Stephen agitated over paperwork at a kitchen table, listening calmly on a couch, sharing a laugh with a colleague over mugs, then sitting quietly among independent people in a public waiting room. Fine gold relational lines shift from jagged to smooth and playful, without a body aura.
page-17.transcript:
Everything radiates something.
Agitation does.
Care does.
The question was never whether I affected the field.
Only how.

page-18.imageDescription: Six cross-cut panels move through Stephen sharing a mug with family, connecting two students, reading a book, considering a star-cluster picture on a laptop, sharing humour with a colleague, and listening as two adults discuss a book and a star-image laptop together. A few fine gold lines bridge panel edges rather than radiating only from Stephen.
page-18.transcript:
Connector.
Not because I knew the final truth.
Because I could sometimes keep two worlds in the same room.

page-19.imageDescription: Five small memory panels (three above two) show Stephen listening at a paper-covered desk, waiting beside a tram, sharing a quiet sofa conversation, participating in a three-person conversation and laughing over mugs. Below, ordinary Stephen stands on a rainy tram platform with his hands in his jacket pockets while independent bystanders wait. Thin gold lines link the memory scenes to the platform; no body aura or costume identity.
page-19.transcript:
Different language. Same shape.
ambient stabiliser
grounded antenna
sanctuary keeper
connector
radiation
Coherence keeper.
Ridiculous.
Still... it fit better than ambition ever had.

page-20.imageDescription: A large Stephen profile raises one hand toward a translucent blue-white curved membrane intersecting his forehead. Around and behind him, three quiet table conversations continue with fine warm-gold relational lines. Three lower insets show him absorbed in star-image laptop research, a book and phone on a tram while a passenger assists an older woman, and home-desk notes while two women talk over mugs behind him. A small closing caption sits in the dark lower margin.
page-20.transcript:
I kept staring at what I couldn’t access.
And almost missed what was already happening.

page-21.imageDescription: In a luminous blue and amber dream, ordinary adult Stephen stands at a vast threshold facing distant indistinct humanlike silhouettes. A small planet hangs on the left. Four translucent edge insets show a sleeping adult face, an open hand, a youthful stargazer and a second view of the threshold. Two quiet narration captions ask about the age of the feeling and the shape recognised by longing.
page-21.transcript:
What if the feeling was older than the story I had about it?
What if ‘volunteer’ was less a memory than a shape the longing recognised?

page-22.imageDescription: Four panels descend from a distant luminous human-shaped figure at a starry threshold to a child becoming ordinary. A curved blue-white forehead membrane is visible against faint architecture, then fades beside a sunlit window. In the final warm room, the child sits on the floor playing with a wooden truck, with a toy basket, books and armchair nearby.
page-22.transcript:
To come all the way in...
you would have to forget enough to become ordinary.
Not pretend to be human.
Be human.

page-23.imageDescription: Five panels alternate cool symbolic forehead-membrane imagery with warm ordinary relationships. Stephen looks through a window, listens to a friend with a mug, faces a starry doorway beside an empty chair, helps a younger adult with an open book, and ends in a calm close-up with the quiet inner-answer echo.
page-23.transcript:
What if doubt wasn’t a flaw in the system?
What if some uncertainty kept the incarnation intact?
to keep you grounded.

page-24.imageDescription: Stephen stands quietly by a rooftop railing under a vast indigo starfield above warm city windows. A faint flowing pair of light lines suggests an almost-heard tune. Four lower sensory insets show gooseflesh on his forearm, his eye, his softened middle-aged face and his relaxed hand resting on the rail.
page-24.transcript:
No memory.
No coordinates.
No proof.
And still... recognition.
Like remembering the shape of a song you can’t quite hear.

page-25.imageDescription: At home Stephen reads the same two brief forum snippets in an establishing laptop view and a close-up, then smiles with a dry thought about backpay. Two dream-office insets show a roster with his name and Brenda stamping a claim beside a huge backpay folder. The page ends quietly with Stephen holding a mug beside his closed laptop and an evening window.
page-25.transcript:
Apparently I wasn’t the only cosmic contractor unhappy with the roster.
last time here
I’m done after this.
last time here
I’m done after this.
The backpay better be enormous.
Stephen
BACKPAY
PENDING.
BRENDA — HR

page-26.imageDescription: Six calm panels show Stephen closing a laptop, walking through a leafy neighbourhood, making a small turn, answering a phone message, holding a door for an older neighbour carrying groceries, and resting on a park bench. A fine gold trail is visible behind the completed turn and a tiny relational line marks the already-held doorway. The final panel is wordless.
page-26.transcript:
Less conquest.
Less demanding the whole map.
A little more sway.
Life presented the next thing.
I answered.

page-27.imageDescription: Five wide ink-drawn panels show Stephen seated on his bed with throat discomfort, a frustrated close face, then a translucent blue-white membrane partly intersecting his forehead. He first touches his forehead, then watches more quietly. In the wordless final panel his relaxed open hand rests beside the intact membrane, with the ordinary bedroom window still visible behind it.
page-27.transcript:
The lock stayed.
So did the old urge to force it.
But the relationship had changed.

page-28.imageDescription: Stephen sits quietly on the bed in a full-page bedroom scene, with a city window, desk, lamp and books. An upper-left inset includes throat sensation; a lower-right inset shows his attentive eye and face. Fine gold and blue-white translucent waves run through the room, figure, starfield overlay and faint head-space membrane. One unboxed GOOOOONG follows the opening wave; three small narration captions lead down into wordless imagery. The membrane is included, not shattered.
page-28.transcript:
GOOOOONG
View.
Waveform.
Then nothing needed naming.

page-29.imageDescription: Four quiet wide panels follow Stephen looking through a thin transparent membrane that intersects head space. Faint stars and remote architecture remain unresolved within it while the normal bedroom and city window become increasingly clear. His expression softens into a small human smile. The final wider view shows him sitting on the bed with the faint contour still present, ordinary furniture and morning light around him.
page-29.transcript:
I still didn’t know where I came from.
But the not-knowing had stopped being a wall.
Recognition was enough for now.

page-30.imageDescription: Two upper panels show Stephen pouring coffee and sharing a warm goodbye with a woman and child. In the large lower panel, wearing a dark hoodie over a grey shirt, he walks naturally through a sunlit neighbourhood among ordinary pedestrians. Faint golden curves pass between everyday interactions; there is no cosmic ascent.
page-30.transcript:
The answer had been annoyingly accurate.
Life.
The lock remained. The wall didn’t.
